questions.question: Examine Booker T. Washington's observations on the relationship between the white and the black people. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• In "A Slave among Slaves," Booker T. Washington portrays the relationship between Black and
  • white people as complex and mutually degraded by the institution of slavery. He highlights the
  • paradoxical loyalty of enslaved people who protected white families during the Civil War and notes
  • a profound lack of vengefulness post-emancipation. Ultimately, Washington observes an irony in
  • their dynamic: slavery left the enslavers helpless and overly dependent, while equipping the
  • formerly enslaved with the practical skills and work ethic necessary to survive and progress
  • independently. [An/CO1]
